messages.subject: ID issues in visualization_sleep.pdf
parts:
Dear Vincent and colleagues,

We are running a project with ~700 participants (with another few hundred on the way) and are planning to investigate sleep questions alongside our physical activity metrics.

One of our first steps for QC on the sleep data is to use the "visualization_sleep" pdf output. It has been incredibly helpful for us in the past, but we are running into an issue with our current study.

Our IDs are structured like this: "Device_serial_number"_"Date_deployed" (e.g., 17-32323_2023- which is too long to fit on the side of the visualization sleep pdf (attached for reference). I have tried re-processing our data using idloc=2 to shorten the IDs, which worked for a subset of our data. However, with larger parts of our dataset, the serial numbers repeat, and GGIR can no longer correctly establish the start and end times for each participant. This gives us a lot more noise to comb through when QC'ing our data with the additional complication of connecting the shortened ID back to the actual participant (since the serial numbers repeat).

Is there a solution for specifying the dimensions or font size of the output for the visualization_sleep file so that our subject IDs are visible next to the sleep plots? We could potentially rig up a solution by creating temporary or different ID's, but I wanted to confirm that there was nothing simpler to be done on the GGIR/visualization side.

Thank you for your help, and please let me know if I can provide any other information!

Best,
Rob

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] ID issues in visualization_sleep.pdf
parts:
Dear Rob,

At the moment GGIR offers no solution, we would have to change the GGIR code to show the ID in a different way.

However, in all studies I have worked with study participants have a unique ID that is separate from the device ID and because of that much shorter. For as far as I know Axivity, ActiGraph and GENEActiv all store the ID at the start of the filename separated by an underscore from the device serial number. So, I think you are better off updating the file names because in that way it will also be easier for your potential collaborators / future users of your data to process it with GGIR or any other software as it is unconventional to use such a long ID.

Best,

Vincent
